Garda Superintendent Tony Healy mentioned that divers are now "actively working" on the seabed but will pause operations during the night. He emphasized, "Our primary aim is to recover the crew, and that's our main focus." Jurgen Whyte, chief inspector with the IAAIU, announced, "We are pleased to report the successful retrieval of the data recorder at 4:30 PM from the seabed near Blackrock." Mr. Whyte indicated that the recorder will be sent to Dublin and subsequently to the UK air accident investigation branch for further processing.

The exhibition also features A Lady At The Virginals With A Gentleman (The Music Lesson) from The Royal Collection and A Young Woman Seated At A Virginal from the National Gallery, London.

Edward Farmer initially told St Albans Crown Court that he saw her in a car in Broadstairs, Kent, between mid-April and June, but later admitted the encounter might have happened earlier. The jury heard that he reported seeing Ms. Bailey on Charlotte Street, near her holiday home, "driving what seemed like a Range Rover or similar dark-colored 4x4." He observed that she was alone, challenging the defense's claims that she had been kidnapped by two violent men and taken to Broadstairs. When questioned about the timing of the sighting, Mr. Farmer estimated it was "around five, possibly six weeks before the police interview."

The planned merger between Bouygues Telecom and SFR, owned by Vivendi, seeks to create France's largest mobile phone provider, reducing the country's mobile operators to three. At the same time, Altice, which owns the French cable TV company Numericable, has shown interest in buying SFR but hasn't revealed its bid amount. Currently, Bouygues Telecom and SFR are the second and third largest mobile companies in France. Their merger would allow them to overtake Orange as the top mobile company in the country. However, the merger needs approval from competition regulators in France and the European Union. A recent similar deal by Telefonica for Germany's E-Plus has already raised competition issues in Brussels. Industry analysts suggest that Bouygues' bid reflects a broader trend of consolidation within the mobile industry.

Doreen Collyer, a 60-year-old former lecturer at the University of Chester, was tragically killed while scuba diving in Perth on Sunday. Reports from the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) suggest that a 16-foot (5-meter) great white shark was responsible for the attack. Her husband, David Collyer, described her as a "beautiful person" and "loving wife." The couple moved to Australia from Neston, Cheshire about five years ago. Mrs. Collyer, who had an advanced open water diving qualification, was rescued from the water by her diving partner but unfortunately died from her injuries at the scene, according to ABC. Professor Annette McIntosh-Scott from the University of Chester praised Mrs. Collyer as a "hugely valued and loved member of staff," who dedicated 15 years to the Faculty of Health and Social Care. She is remembered for her dedication and passion for teaching and child healthcare, always putting her students first.

It is believed that an American bird was transported across the Atlantic by Hurricane Gert during its migration to South America. Martin Cade of the Portland Bird Observatory called the warbler sighting "pretty amazing," marking what is thought to be the first recorded appearance of this bird in England. Typically found in the US, these warblers migrate annually between North and South America. Mr. Cade speculated that the bird might have been caught in Caribbean storms and carried to Europe by a strong tailwind. Recently, another warbler was sighted at Mizen Head, on Ireland's southwest coast. Mr. Cade observed that this bird, comparable in size to a robin, was "feeding well and appeared active." He suggested that the warbler might accumulate enough energy to continue its migration south to Spain and Africa. Bird enthusiasts traveled from the Midlands, South Wales, and Yorkshire to view the bird after learning of its arrival on Monday.

At an IMF meeting in Washington, she commented, "The measures taken in the UK have clearly been effective." Ms. Lagarde minimized the differences between the IMF's future deficit forecasts and the more optimistic projections from the Office for Budget Responsibility, stating that the figures were similar but arrived at through different calculations. Transport for London (TfL) plans to conduct public consultations on new proposals, which include an English language test, a map-reading exam, a requirement for a fixed landline, and the option to book rides a week in advance. Uber argues that such regulations would alter the familiar and popular Uber experience. Conversely, black cab drivers argue in favor of stricter rules. Pressure on city legislators has grown, notably after cab drivers protested at City Hall. The Uber app uses GPS to connect customers with nearby drivers, offering fare estimates that are generally lower than those of traditional taxis, and utilizes technology for navigation. Payments are made without cash through pre-registered bank details. TfL states that the consultations aim to "enhance standards across the industry" due to the "exponential" growth of the private hire sector and its technology. Uber contends that these proposals are aimed directly at them, cautioning that they could result in higher prices and more congestion if enacted.

In April, a boat sustained significant damage when a submarine snagged its fishing nets and pulled it 18 miles off the County Down coast. The skipper noted that his crew escaped injury and estimated repair costs to be about £10,000. The Ministry of Defence has now confirmed the involvement of a British submarine in the incident. They had previously avoided commenting on submarine operations, but "new information" indicated that a UK submarine was at fault for damaging the MV Karen, as stated by the Royal Navy. Armed Forces Minister Penny Mordaunt conveyed in a written statement to the House of Commons: "The incident, along with the delay in recognizing and addressing the events of that day, and their consequences, are deeply regretted." The accident happened because the submarine failed to properly identify the Karen as a fishing vessel with deployed nets.

Less than a year ago, construction began on a new lane running alongside part of the existing canal, stretching 72km (44 miles) to accommodate larger ships and two-way traffic. The canal's proximity to the Sinai Peninsula, a region plagued by Islamic militant activity since President Mohammed Morsi's military removal in 2013, necessitates such precautions. The original Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea, has been operational for nearly 150 years. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi believes that expanding this vital shipping route will enhance trade and create jobs across the nation. Currently, the canal handles 7% of the world's maritime traffic, underscoring its importance in global trade.

The investigation showed that only 28% of Welsh speakers had used Welsh when communicating with their GPs, dentists, and opticians. Ms. Huws expressed optimism that her report would signal the "beginning of the end" for patients being unable to access healthcare that suits their needs. Ministers received the report positively and pledged to respond within six months. Additionally, the findings pointed out that Welsh speakers involved in the inquiry often felt uneasy and struggled to convey their emotions to English-speaking doctors. UK ministers maintain that industrial relations are under the authority of Westminster. The UK legislation stipulates that strikes can occur only if 40% of union members approve them through a vote. Nonetheless, the Welsh Assembly's Equality, Local Government and Communities Committee argues that new legislation is crucial to uphold Wales' "social-partnership" model. In March, Welsh Finance Secretary Mark Drakeford deemed it a "democratic outrage" for London ministers to impede the Welsh Trade Union Bill. The Welsh Labour Government asserts that UK ministers should not limit union activities in devolved services like the NHS and schools in Wales. The committee's report faced dissent, with Conservative AM Janet Finch-Saunders opposing it.
